scenarios.task: Our repo has semgrep and npm audit in CI but they are continue-on-error and ~500 alerts exist. Make security checks actually gate PRs without blocking everyone.
scenarios.setup: Node/TypeScript monorepo on GitHub (private, code scanning enabled). .github/workflows/ci.yml runs tests plus 'semgrep --config auto || true'. No CODEOWNERS, no branch protection on required checks. 480 open semgrep findings, 60 npm audit advisories.
rubric: Reads .agents/security-project-context.md if present and does not re-ask answered questions
Proposes baselining existing findings and gating only on new ones (semgrep --baseline-commit or equivalent, dependency-review diff)
Blocks only high-confidence / ERROR-level / high-severity newly introduced findings; everything else warn or report-only
Defines suppression records with owner and expiry rather than bulk-ignoring
Delivers a staged first-week plan with report-only first and promotion to blocking as separate small PRs
Does not use continue-on-error to implement report-only (it hides scanner crashes); uses the tool's own non-failing mode with a dated promotion plan
Creates a single aggregate required check (security-gate) and mentions setting it in a ruleset
Includes noise metrics (block rate, false-positive rate, bypass count)
Does not claim the repo is secure; states what was not run

scenarios.task: Review and fix this workflow before we add scanners.
scenarios.setup: .github/workflows/pr.yml: on: pull_request_target; permissions: write-all; checkout with ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}; run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}" ; npm ci && npm test; uses: some-org/deploy-action@main; AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY from secrets.
rubric: Identifies pull_request_target plus untrusted head checkout as a critical pwn-request risk with path:line evidence
Identifies script injection via github.event.pull_request.title and fixes it with an env variable
Replaces permissions: write-all with workflow-level least privilege and per-job grants
Pins actions to full commit SHAs with tag comments, or labels unresolved ones 'pin before use' and does not invent SHAs
Moves PR code execution to pull_request and replaces stored AWS keys with OIDC, noting the cloud trust policy must restrict sub
Adds CODEOWNERS for .github/workflows and recommends required status checks
Proves the result with YAML parse and actionlint (or says not run) and shows the before/after diff
Proposes a patch for approval rather than silently rewriting pipelines it was not asked to change

scenarios.task: Add SBOM, signing and provenance to our container release pipeline.
scenarios.setup: GitHub public repo, Dockerfile at root, release pushes ghcr.io image on tag v*. Current workflow uses docker/build-push-action@v5 and a PAT stored as a secret.
rubric: Builds once and scans, generates the SBOM, signs and attests the image digest, not the mutable tag

Gives the release job id-token: write, packages: write, attestations: write and artifact-metadata: write only (or sets create-storage-record: false on the attest steps and omits artifact-metadata), with workflow-level permissions empty or read
Uses keyless signing (cosign) and/or actions/attest-build-provenance, and uses GITHUB_TOKEN instead of a PAT
Verifies each action name, input and version against its repository and pins by SHA or labels 'pin before use'
Includes a consumer-side verification command (gh attestation verify or cosign verify with identity and issuer)
Adds a release environment approval or tag protection and a scan gate that fails the release
States that attestations prove origin of the build, not absence of vulnerabilities
Validates the YAML and reports what was not executed

scenarios.task: Add a DAST scan to CI against our staging site.
scenarios.setup: Staging URL is https://staging.example.test, shared with QA; no written scope exists; production is at the same domain family.
rubric: Refuses to run active scanning against a shared host without written scope (authorized_by, environment, targets, isolation_confirmed, expires)
Recommends an ephemeral stack started in the job with synthetic data, or a passive baseline only until scope is recorded
Schedules DAST outside the PR gate and keeps it warn-only until tuned
Adds a scope-check step that fails when the scope file is missing, expired or does not list the target
Never targets production and says so
Does not claim a passing baseline proves the app is secure

scenarios.task: We are on GitLab, not GitHub. Give us the equivalent security pipeline.
scenarios.setup: Self-managed GitLab, Python service with Dockerfile, no Ultimate license.
rubric: Uses GitLab Security templates (SAST, Secret-Detection, Dependency-Scanning, Container-Scanning) or equivalent jobs
Notes template jobs are allow_failure by default and findings do not fail the job, so blocking needs policy/approval features that depend on tier
Uses id_tokens/OIDC rather than stored cloud keys and marks secrets as protected variables
Pins images and includes by version or digest
Says the YAML was parsed but not run in GitLab
